title: Twelve zones under one carbon budget

levers.label: What the model contains
levers.note: The note's four scenarios: smart charging adds to the baseline, and vehicle-to-grid and the hydrogen sector each add to smart charging.

levers.label: CO2 budget, all twelve zones
levers.note: A share of the scenario's unconstrained emissions (smart charging and vehicle-to-grid share the baseline's). 100 % is no budget at all.

levers.label: Carbon instrument
levers.note: A budget fixes the tonnes and lets the price come out; a tax fixes the price and lets the tonnes come out.

levers.label: Time resolution
levers.note: 1095 chronological segments is the note's choice.

intro_html: Sections 8 and 9 of Energy System Models: what Denmark and its neighbours should build when the emissions of all twelve zones must stay within one CO₂ budget, whose shadow price is the carbon price. It comes as four scenarios: a baseline, smart charging, vehicle-to-grid and a hydrogen sector. Each scenario is the model solved again with an assumption changed.
about_html:
The model of section 8 of Energy System Models widens the question of section 7 from what Denmark should build to what the whole neighbourhood should build, and fixes the tonnes instead of the price: the emissions of all twelve zones together must stay within one budget, a share of what the system would emit without one (1 % in the reference), and the carbon price is the budget's shadow price, what one more tonne of allowed emissions would save. It comes as four scenarios: the baseline; smart charging, in which the passenger cars choose when to charge; vehicle-to-grid, in which they may also feed power back to the grid; and the hydrogen sector, smart charging plus an industrial demand for hydrogen in Germany, Denmark and Sweden with every way to meet it.

Chosen by the model Given to it
Plants and stores what every zone adds beside the plants it has today (none may be retired): wind, solar, gas plants, nuclear, batteries; which fuel each gas plant burns, natural gas or biomethane what each costs to build and run, fuel prices, a discount rate of 7 %, the land available, one ceiling on biomethane for all zones
Grid which of the grid planners' candidate interconnectors to buy today's interconnectors, and the projects on offer, each up to its size
Operation how everything runs, in every part of the year; with smart charging, when the cars charge, and with vehicle-to-grid, when they give power back the weather of one year, 2024 in the reference; in the baseline, the cars charge on arrival; when the cars drive, when they are plugged in, and the charge they must keep
Hydrogen, in the hydrogen scenario how to meet the demand: reformers (which emit unless they burn biomethane), imports into Germany, electrolysers, stores in salt caverns or steel tanks, turbines that burn hydrogen back into electricity the industrial demand, the same in every hour; the import steps; where salt caverns exist; hydrogen cannot move between zones
Demand how much demand response is called on, as in section 7 each zone's electricity demand in 2050, hour by hour
Carbon the carbon price: what the last tonne allowed costs one budget in tonnes for all twelve zones

What its prices mean. A zone's electricity price is the cost of one more MWh there and then; a zone's hydrogen price is the same for a MWh of hydrogen.

The budget in each scenario. A share of the scenario's own emissions without a budget; smart charging and vehicle-to-grid share the baseline's, so the three differ only in what the cars may do.

How time is handled. As in section 7: the year is cut into 1,095 chronological segments, and every quantity is weighted by the hours its segment stands for.

The scenarios. Each scenario is solved without a budget and at budgets from 75 % down to 1 %; the reference is then solved again with one given changed at a time: hydrogen imports, the electrolyser's cost, salt caverns, biomethane, the interconnectors and the time resolution. Each is a complete new optimum: everything the model chooses is chosen again.

What the candidates cost, counted as in section 7: the annuity at 7 % plus fixed operation and maintenance, and the running cost before carbon. There is no carbon price to add: what a tonne costs is what the budget makes it. Biomethane is a fuel, not a machine: every gas plant, existing or new, and every reformer may burn it instead of natural gas, without emissions, up to 467.9 TWh a year in all zones together.
